rounds.text: Allcargo Terminals Ltd demonstrates robust profitability metrics that clearly surpass sector benchmarks, delivering an ROE of 12.54% against a sector benchmark of 5.31% and an ROA of 3.32% compared to a sector benchmark of 2.89% [E8, E9]. Operational efficiency is exceptionally strong, backed by a yearly operating-margin trend that has been increasing over the last 4 years alongside a quarterly operating-margin trend increasing over the last 10 quarters [E25, E26]. This margin expansion is tangible, with operating margin reaching 21% in TTM compared to 16% three years earlier and 22% in June 2026 versus 18% in the year-ago quarter [E23, E24]. Furthermore, cash generation is extraordinary, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of 3.57x for March 2026 where profits are fully backed by cash, resulting in Rs 157 Cr of operating cash flow and Rs 145 Cr of free cash flow [E27, E28, E29]. Technical momentum also supports the underlying business strength, as the share price sits above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with the 50-day above the 200-day [E43], accompanied by positive institutional money flow [E37]. Conceded: debt exceeds net worth with a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.18x and borrowings rising to Rs 769 Cr [E30, E32].

The evidence reveals a heavy balance-sheet risk, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.18x as of March 2026 where borrowings have surged to Rs 769 Cr from Rs 548 Cr a year prior, leading to explicit warnings of low interest coverage [E30, E32, E53]. Valuation is heavily detached from intrinsic value, as a discounted cash flow model sets the intrinsic value at Rs 16 against a market price of Rs 25.9, resulting in a severe negative margin of safety of -66.4% and an overvaluation flag [E38, E39, E61, E62]. Long-term wealth creation for shareholders has lagged badly, underscored by a 3-year compounded profit growth of -12% alongside 3-year and 1-year compounded share price declines of -14% and -21% respectively [E16, E18, E19]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is eroding through steady promoter and institutional stake reductions, with promoter holdings dropping from 69.91% in December 2023 to 67.17% in September 2026, foreign institutional holdings falling from 7.61% to 5.36%, and domestic institutional holdings sliding from 0.75% to 0.21% [E34, E35, E36]. The equity also yields 0.00% in dividends despite repeated reporting of profits, prompting direct flags regarding shareholder returns [E4, E52]. Conceded: operating margins have expanded to 21% in TTM and quarterly cash conversion stands robustly at 3.57x [E23, E27].

Conceded: debt-to-equity is 2.18x with borrowings at Rs 769 Cr [E30, E32], and the DCF model indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 16 against the current price [E38]. However, the bear's focus on historical profit declines overlooks explosive recent momentum, evidenced by a TTM compounded profit growth of 31% [E17] and a TTM sales growth of 12% [E15]. The bear's claim of eroding institutional confidence ignores the positive money flow signal showing net institutional accumulation [E37]. Furthermore, operating margins have demonstrably expanded to 21% in the TTM alongside a multi-year and 10-quarter rising margin trend [E23, E25, E26]. Finally, profits are fully backed by cash with an exceptional cash conversion ratio of 3.57x, yielding Rs 145 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E27, E29].

Conceded: TTM compounded profit growth reached 31% [E17] and TTM sales growth is 12% [E15]. However, that short-term acceleration ignores a multi-year trend of financial contraction, specifically a 3-year compounded profit growth of -12% [E16] alongside negative 3-year (-14%) and 1-year (-21%) share price growth [E18, E19]. Conceded: the institutional signal shows a minor positive money flow of +0.02 percentage points [E37]. Yet, that single metric fails to refute the broader multi-quarter institutional exodus, where promoter holding dropped from 69.91% to 67.17%, foreign institutional holding fell from 7.61% to 5.36%, and domestic institutional holding plunged from 0.75% to 0.21% [E34, E35, E36]. While operating margins and cash flows improved [E23, E29], they fail to neutralize the severe leverage risk posed by borrowings rising to Rs 769 Cr alongside a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.18x [E30, E32], a low interest coverage flag [E53], and a zero dividend yield [E4] that offers shareholders no cash return despite reported profits.
